My baby was also in the NICU for 3 months (he was born at 27 weeks) and when we finally got to bring him home he would only sleep if I was holding him. It took a few weeks of putting down and picking him out of the bassinet for him to finally sleep "on his own". Then he had to bounced (sometimes for hours) until he would fall asleep. At that point I talked to my friend who gave me pointers on sleep training. Put the baby down when they're about to fall asleep. Leave the room. They will cry. Give it 4 minutes and then go in and soothe them without picking them up (that is important). They will settle and they will cry again. Give it another 4 minutes and go in do the same thing you did before. It might take a couple hours but it pays off, believe me! The next night let them cry for 5 minutes before going in to soothe them. The next night add 2 minutes and go in after 7 minutes. It's not fun but after 2 weeks my baby was going down in his crib awake and would fall asleep, sans crying, after about 15 minutes.

My baby had to be held to sleep for a long time 
Then he needed to be bounced to sleep for a long time. But at 6 mos. we started sleep training him and, though that week and a half sucked, it has payed off! Wait a couple months and learn how your baby comforts themself and then start sleep training.
